transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello — do you have any questions about your cataract surgery or recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. I'm wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
You can go back to light exercise after 1 week, and that includes gardening. Please avoid heavy work, lifting, and swimming for a month.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for that information. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
If you were using eye drops before your operation, such as for dry eyes, it’s safe to continue using them unless you’ve been told otherwise. If you’re running out, your GP should be able to provide more.  

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That’s really helpful to know, thank you. Another thing I've noticed is that I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Some sensitivity to light can be normal as your eye adjusts to the new lens. If it is mild and things just seem brighter than you’re used to, wearing sunglasses outside is recommended. But significant pain in bright light, or severe light sensitivity, is not normal — especially if the eye is also red and painful — and we may need to assess this further.  

Do you have any other questions?
